papers.title: Quantum-Information Probes of Collapse Dynamics in Causal Fermion Systems
papers.abstract: Finster, Kleiner, and Paganini derived from causal fermion systems (CFS) a nonrelativistic effective collapse model whose statistical operator obeys, to leading order, a Kossakowski--Lindblad equation. In the factorized regime of that derivation, the dissipator is built from purely spatial operators $N_{k,a}$ with positive rates fixed by microscopic time-nonlocal kernels. We translate this CFS-specific generator into quantities accessible to coherent quantum processors. The resulting CFS Dirichlet form obeys an exact purity-loss identity under arbitrary Hamiltonian control, and its null algebra is the commutant of the $*$-algebra generated by the projected $N_{k,a}$. For joint eigenbranches we obtain an exact distinguishability functional controlling exponential coherence loss and a lower bound on channel distance from ideal unitary evolution. In an $n$-qubit dephasing sector, the projected kernels generate a positive-semidefinite covariance matrix $C$, with GHZ visibility $\exp[-2T\bm{1}^{\mathsf T}C\bm{1}]$. We prove that uniformly summable finite-range correlations yield at most $O(n)$ GHZ decay, whereas $O(n^2)$ scaling requires a collective non-summable component. Single- and two-qubit cat coherences reconstruct $C$, giving a covariance-spectroscopy protocol, while Knill--Laflamme conditions characterize first-order correctability of the projected CFS error algebra. We also derive an explicit compatibility inequality between macroscopic state reduction and long coherent computation and show why absence of probe heating does not imply absence of coherence signatures. The results do not exclude CFS: its covariance strength, $\ellmin$, and hardware projection remain underdetermined. They instead identify the microscopic input required for a genuine no-go theorem and establish scalable quantum processors as direct probes of the CFS collapse sector.

papers.title: Isomorphism Loci and Coherence in Equivalence Extension
papers.abstract: We study the restriction data carried by dependent-product extension along a monomorphism. In a locally cartesian closed category, the extended map is an isomorphism after a change of base if and only if the input map is an isomorphism on the restricted base. In a topos, its isomorphism locus is therefore the universal quantification of the input locus. A terminal characterization gives coherent comparisons for base change and successive extension, together with formulas for intersections and unions. Under explicit homotopical, cartesian, and universe hypotheses, this construction gives equivalence extension and preserves the boundary identifications used to prove fibrancy of a universe. Graph comparisons and strict fillers of a fixed universe boundary are represented by trivially fibrant objects. A single realignment over the comparison object induces a weak equivalence between these parameter objects, and both admit extensions of every finite cubical boundary. A finite-groupoid example shows that graph comparisons cannot be selected naturally under all isomorphisms of unstructured input.

papers.title: A boundary limit for Suzuki's arithmetic canonical system
papers.abstract: For the shifted Riemann xi-function, we prove the large-radius boundary limit of Suzuki's arithmetic canonical system. The proof applies to every positive shift for which the reflected quotient is pole-free in the upper half-plane and the two entire functions have no common zero. It therefore applies unconditionally to shifts at least one half, including Suzuki's original range greater than one. We give the weak-kernel construction needed at the smaller shifts, two integral identities for its positive determinant ratio, and decay estimates faster than every fixed exponential in logarithmic radius. The hypotheses on the shift are retained throughout.

papers.title: A congruence obstruction to Ibn al-Khawwām’s eleventh problem
papers.abstract: We prove that there are no two rational squares whose sum is ten and such that adding its own square root to each gives another rational square. This is the existence question in Ibn al-Khawwām’s eleventh arithmetic problem. The proof uses only the residues of squares modulo three and a divisibility argument.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Foregger-Sinkhorn tie-point conjecture
papers.abstract: The Foregger-Sinkhorn tie-point conjecture asserts that if a nearly decomposable doubly stochastic matrix minimizes the permanent on a face and the permanental cofactor at a prescribed zero is larger than its permanent, then that zero is a tie point. We give a counterexample in dimension eight.

papers.title: A Fibonacci Analogue of the Fifteen Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove that a positive-definite quadratic form with integral Gram matrix represents every Fibonacci number if and only if it represents the first forty-two of them. The unique minimal criterion set consists of ten Fibonacci numbers, the largest of which is $F_{42}=267914296$.

papers.title: A formal proof in Lean of the finiteness of planar five-body central configurations for all positive masses
papers.abstract: Smale's sixth problem asks whether, for every choice of positive masses, there are finitely many central configurations up to similarity. For five bodies in the plane, Albouy and Kaloshin proved finiteness outside a set of masses of codimension two. In a companion paper the author proved finiteness for every choice of five positive masses by their method, adding steps that cannot be checked by hand: exact computer algebra, rational certificates and a branch and bound. We formalize this theorem in Lean 4 with Mathlib without assuming the results of Albouy and Kaloshin that the informal proof uses. Instead we prove what the proof needs of their rules on limit diagrams, of their classification of these diagrams and of their mass conditions. We do so at places of complex algebraic curves, taken as valuations of the function field rather than points of a projective model. Almost every computation becomes data for a checker that we write in Lean, prove sound with respect to Mathlib's real and complex numbers, and run in the kernel (proof by reflection). The main theorem depends on about $680{,}000$ theorems proved in this way, and Mathlib's tactics prove the few other computations. The proof uses only Lean's three standard axioms, and two independent Lean kernels, nanoda and lean4lean, accept it.

papers.title: A Lean 4 formalization of the area law for three-dimensional U(1) lattice gauge theory with the Wilson action
papers.abstract: In three-dimensional $U(1)$ lattice gauge theory with the Wilson action, static charges are confined at every coupling: rectangular Wilson loops obey an area law, uniformly in the finite box. This was proved recently by the author in a separate paper; the proof runs to over three hundred pages with its supplement and adapts the Debye-screening analysis of Brydges and Federbush and the multiscale expansion of Göpfert and Mack. We describe a formalization of this proof in Lean 4 with Mathlib, which also covers the paper's corollaries and its appendix on comparing Wilson and Villain loops. The formal theorems take no hypotheses and use only the standard axioms of Lean. The proof became formalizable through explicit interfaces between its parts, written-out versions of the steps that the paper adapts from the literature or leaves out, and certified values for every numerical constant. The formalization also yielded 70 corrections and improvements to the paper, none of which changes its main results.

papers.title: A lower bound of 0.8366 for Lebesgue's universal covering problem
papers.abstract: A universal cover is a convex set in the plane that contains a congruent copy of every set of diameter at most $1$. Lebesgue asked in 1914 for a universal cover of least area; before this work, the infimum $\Lambda$ of the areas of universal covers was known to satisfy $0.83474\le\Lambda\le0.8441$. Lower bounds come from test sets: $\Lambda$ is bounded below by the least area of a convex hull of congruent copies of given sets of diameter at most $1$. The best earlier lower bounds used the disk, the Reuleaux triangle and the Reuleaux pentagon, but these three bodies are known to admit a placement with hull area below $0.83479$, so they cannot give a much better bound. Adding the regular Reuleaux heptagon and nonagon of width $1$, we improve the lower bound to $\Lambda\ge0.8366$. Without the nonagon, the other four bodies already give $\Lambda\ge0.836$. The proof is a computer-assisted branch and bound over the relative placements of the bodies. Its certificates are checked in interval arithmetic, and separate proofs of both bounds in Lean 4, with their own certificates, are checked entirely by Lean's kernel.

papers.title: A proof that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$ through congruent-number twists
papers.abstract: We give a proof of Glazer and collaborators' theorem that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$, which builds on OpenAI's proof that Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$ has a negative answer. Integers are represented by multiples of a point on an elliptic curve of rank one over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$. An existential condition on two congruent-number twists forbids poles of odd order at odd primes. A height bound at six rational points, from a quaternionic Shimura curve and Serre's conjecture (a theorem of Khare–Wintenberger and Kisin), and a prime pattern from the Green–Tao–Ziegler theorem turn congruences at chosen primes into identities between multiples, and the growth of a Lucas sequence forces integrality. Our contribution is the existence of the rational points that the condition on twists requires: for coprime squarefree integers $\beta>1$ and $\theta\ge1$ with $\beta\equiv\theta\equiv1\pmod8$, each a square modulo the primes of the other, there is an integer $e$ such that $y^2=x^3-e^2x$ and $y^2=x^3-e^2\theta^2x$ both have rank one and a rational point with abscissa in $\beta\mathbb{Q}^{\times2}$. Where Glazer and collaborators use a restricted $2$-converse theorem, this rests on published theorems: the genus criterion of Tian, Yuan and Zhang, with Gross–Zagier.

papers.title: A superlogarithmic lower bound for deterministic word separation
papers.abstract: Let $S(n)$ be the maximum, over distinct binary words of length $n$, of the least number of states in a complete deterministic finite automaton that accepts exactly one of them. We prove $S(n)\geq(1-o(1))\log n\log\log n$. The main step is a common word of length $\exp(O(\sqrt{k}\log k))$ that, after suitable powering of the generators, reaches the sink components of every transformation pair on $k$ states and attains minimum rank on each sink. This transfers the balanced positive permutation identities of Xu and Regan to the full transformation monoid without changing their leading logarithmic length. The conclusion concerns deterministic automata; it makes no assertion about nondeterministic separators.

papers.title: A thrackle on n vertices has fewer than 4n/3 edges
papers.abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every two edges meet exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that a thrackle with $n$ vertices has at most $n$ edges. We prove that a thrackle with $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\frac43(n-1)$ edges, improving the bound $\frac{18}{13}(n-1)$ obtained by Tóth and, independently, by Scoppetto. The proof combines Xu's discharging argument with two computer searches, by the method of Fulek and Pach, showing that two generalized dumbbells in the sense of Fulek and Pach are not thrackleable: $\mathrm{DB}(6,8,-1)$ is a $6$-cycle and an $8$-cycle sharing one edge; $\mathrm{DB}(6,10,-3)$ is a $6$-cycle and a $10$-cycle sharing a path of three edges. A formal proof in Lean 4 derives the bound from five properties of thrackles and checks the computational facts it uses; Section 6 states what this proof trusts.

papers.title: A unimodular continued fraction for cubic irrationals
papers.abstract: We construct a single algorithm that assigns to every real number a recoverable sequence of positive integers which is eventually periodic exactly when the input is a cubic irrational. Its matrix digits are positive unimodular transformations on the two-dimensional simplex. Their products determine nested rational triangles whose diameters decrease by at least a factor of two at each step. An effectively specified partition combines Euclidean reduction with the dominant eigenvectors of cubic units. In both cubic signatures the matrix expansion eventually repeats a single matrix, whose Perron eigenvalue is a unit generating the input field.

papers.title: An effective André–Oort theorem for Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: We give effective bounds for the special subvarieties $V$ that are maximal in a subvariety $Z$ of a Shimura variety, in terms of the degree of $Z$: for the degree of $V$, with no hypothesis; and for the discriminant of a number field $L_V$ attached to $V$ and the Klingler–Yafaev invariant $\alpha_V$ of the level, if for some $\delta>0$ the Dedekind zeta function of $L_V$ has no zero with real part greater than $1-\delta$. Here $Z$ is geometrically irreducible and defined over a number field, the level is neat and of product form, and the bounds are explicit in the degree of $Z$ and, for $L_V$ and $\alpha_V$, also in the degree of the field and $\delta$, with constants that are effectively computable from the Shimura datum, the level and representatives of the connected components of the adjoint Shimura variety. A preprint of Cureton and Thorner, whose proof has been formalized in Lean, establishes such a half-plane with $\delta=1/32$ for every number field; granting it, all these bounds hold with no further hypothesis. For abelian type, an algorithm lists these subvarieties from the bounds, given a finite étale cover by a Shimura variety of Hodge type inside one of Mumford's moduli spaces and equations for the preimage of $Z$.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of Fundamental Theorem of Algebra over Rationals
papers.abstract: We, with the aid of AI, give an elementary proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra over Rationals, i.e., for any nonconstant polynomial $f$ with rational complex number coefficients and every positive rational number $\eps$, there exists a rational complex number $z$ such that $Q(f(z))<\eps^2$. The proof is constructive and relies only on finite rational arithmetic, without using real numbers, infinite sets, or related concepts.

papers.title: An ergodic classification of smooth type subshifts over odd two-letter alphabets
papers.abstract: Fix distinct positive odd integers $\alpha<\beta$. We classify the invariant probability measures of the smooth subshifts obtained by prescribing the successive run types. Every such subshift is uniquely ergodic if $\alpha\ge3$ or $\{\alpha,\beta\}=\{1,3\},\{1,5\}$. For $\alpha=1$ and $\beta\ge7$, unique ergodicity holds exactly for directives containing infinitely many zeros; every other directive gives precisely two ergodic measures. The proof combines a two-dimensional frequency recursion with recognized run decompositions and explicit control of the density of decomposition boundaries.

papers.title: An Explicit Lower Bound for the Proportion of Isolated Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We study isolation in the full sequence of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with positive ordinate, counted with multiplicity. For every fixed $0<c\le10^{-5}$, we prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of zeros whose two neighboring gaps both exceed $2\pi c/\log X$ is at least $0.672468$. Here $X$ is the common height cutoff and the neighbors are taken from the infinite sequence. This refines Lamzouri's small-fixed-gap bound $0.6552\ldots$. We retain his isolation argument and the Montgomery–Taylor kernel, while replacing the linear cost of horizontal displacement by a certified majorant with a positive threshold. Young's shifted mollified second moment bounds the corresponding truncated displacement moment. We supply the boundary and global-height arguments and obtain a gap loss $6\pi^2c^2$ uniform under the required smoothing. A fixed interval-arithmetic certificate completes the numerical estimate. The result is asymptotic and gives no effective first height.

papers.title: An Unconditional Artin-Matthews Theorem For Simultaneous Primitive Roots
papers.abstract: Let S be a finite set of integers diﬀerent from 0 and ±1. We prove that the primes for which every member of S is a primitive root have positive lower relative density precisely when neither of Matthews’ two obstructions occurs. The proof uses the marked estimates for prime predecessors and uniform splitting estimates of OpenAI. Its principal step is a refinement of the large-prime-factor law for prime predecessors by a fixed cubic Frobenius condition. We obtain this refinement from a shifted bilinear estimate for cubic theta series, a divisor-weighted positive sieve estimate, and a prime-extraction argument that retains the natural Hecke coeﬃcients. The resulting lower bound holds in every suﬃciently large dyadic interval.

papers.title: At least one of β(4), β(6), …, β(32) is irrational
papers.abstract: For the Dirichlet beta function, we prove that at least one of $\beta(4),\beta(6),\ldots,\beta(32)$ is irrational. This reduces Krisman's seventeen-value set $\beta(4),\beta(6),\ldots,\beta(36)$ (Hexagon 2610.00285v2) to fifteen values. The improvement comes from a sharper denominator estimate for his construction.

papers.title: Automorphic realization of Langlands parameters for split groups over global function fields, I. Arithmetic foundations and the main theorems
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a split connected reductive group over a global function field \(F\). V. Lafforgue decomposed the space of cusp forms on \(G\) according to semisimple Langlands parameters. This is the first of three papers which prove a converse: every semisimple elliptic parameter is the parameter of a cusp form on \(G\) over \(F\) itself, which we call an automorphic realization of the parameter. This holds in every positive characteristic for classical groups, in characteristic greater than \(3\) for \(G_2\) and \(F_4\), greater than \(5\) for \(E_6\), and greater than \(7\) for \(E_7\) and \(E_8\). A parameter that is not elliptic is the parameter of an automorphic form which is not cuspidal, under the bound for the smallest Levi subgroup through which the parameter factors. The form has the prescribed eigenvalue for every excursion operator, and we determine for which lattices in the centre it can be taken invariant. The present paper contains the arithmetic part of the proof. It defines excursion operators on functions that are not assumed cuspidal, proves their compatibility with constant terms, shows that a function on which they act through an elliptic parameter is a cusp form, and passes from simply connected groups to isogenous groups and from Levi subgroups to the group. This reduces the theorems to the existence of a cusp form with a given elliptic parameter on a simply connected simple group. That is proved in the second paper by a geometric method, when the characteristic does not divide the order of the Weyl group, and in the third paper for classical groups, by descent from general linear groups.

papers.title: Bootstrapping GAGA Theorems
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a noetherian scheme with affine diagonal, and let $\lambda : \mathcal{X} \to X$ be a morphism of locally ringed spaces from a qcqs locally strongly noetherian analytic adic space. We prove that an equivalence on coherent sheaves, together with comparison of their cohomology, extends to every proper $X$-scheme. As an application, we obtain GAGA for proper schemes over the Fargues--Fontaine curve in equal and mixed characteristic.

papers.title: Borel Ruziewicz problem
papers.abstract: We prove that normalized surface measure is the unique finitely additive rotation-invariant probability on the Borel subsets of $S^n$, $n\geq2$. We also prove that Lebesgue measure is the unique finitely additive measure on bounded Borel subsets of $\R^d$, $d\geq3$, invariant under orientation-preserving rigid motions and normalized on the unit cube. The main step is the annihilation of Borel null sets. A spectral gap first gives bounded divergence certificates for compact null sets, chosen in a jointly Borel way. A shared random threshold then combines these certificates to cover arbitrary null sets. For Euclidean space, the construction is applied to families of spheres about two centers; spherical averaging completes the identification of the measure.

papers.title: Causal prediction of rare recovery responses and the optimal scale of observation time
papers.abstract: We determine the information and physical waiting needed to predict a rare intervention response with error smaller than its occurrence probability in a one-dimensional growth process with renewed Poisson interval catastrophes. Deletions of initial sources in macroscopic intervals define a mixed response, with all intervention arms sharing the same stationary past and future forcing. A fixed number of growing submacroscopic gaps determines its rare-event probability scale. We identify the response probability and amplitude, characterize when terminal extinction bits lose predictive information, and construct a gate that recovers this information from the recovery trajectory. For absolute and squared loss, a deterministic-age Bayes-risk expansion holds uniformly with additive error smaller than the rare-event probability. Our main waiting theorem covers every honest causal stopping rule, allowing the complete realized catastrophe history. Its average-time benchmark is the sum of each ordered gap length weighted by the extinction probabilities of preceding gaps. Prediction error smaller than the rare-event probability requires mean waiting divided by this benchmark to diverge; every prescribed diverging multiplier is achievable using actual recovery records. With gap scales $n^{2/5}$ and $n^{4/5}$ and integrated catastrophe tail $A_x\sim C/x$, deterministic observation requires age larger than the $n^{4/5}$ scale, whereas a stopping rule achieves mean waiting $O(n^{2/5}\log n)$. The proofs preserve the rare-event scale through weighted response approximation, risk transfer over arbitrary information fields, and posterior lower bounds on rare history branches.

papers.title: Certified lower bounds for the first and the signed third autocorrelation constants
papers.abstract: Let $C_1$ be the largest constant such that $\sup_{|t|\le 1/2}\int f(t-x)f(x)\,dx\ge C_1\bigl(\int_{-1/4}^{1/4}f\bigr)^2$ for every nonnegative function $f$ on the real line. We prove $C_1\ge 1.337$, improving the bound $1.2937$ of Kim and Pilanci, by a spatial branch-and-bound over the masses of $f$ on equal bins. Consequently, for every large $g$, every $g$-Sidon set in $\{1,\dots,N\}$ has fewer than $1.2231\sqrt{gN}$ elements once $N$ is large enough in terms of $g$. For real-valued $f$ supported in $[-1/4,1/4]$, let $C_3$ and $C_3'$ be the analogous constants for the essential suprema of $|f*f|$ and of $f*f$; no lower bound better than the trivial bound $1$ was recorded for them. We prove $C_3\ge C_3'\ge 4/3$ with the argument principle. Both proofs are computer-assisted, and both theorems are also proved in Lean 4.

papers.title: Certified lower bounds on the optimal-decoding threshold of the surface code
papers.abstract: Under independent bit flips, rigorous lower bounds on the threshold of the surface code from earlier work stay below $0.04$, while numerical estimates place the optimal threshold near $0.109$. By counting labelled failure paths with exact transfer-matrix certificates, we prove without sampling that every minimum-weight decoder has threshold at least $0.0465$ on the planar and rotated codes. We then give statistical certificates that, with confidence $1-10^{-9}$ each, the optimal threshold of the planar code is at least $0.103$ under bit flips and at least $0.02$ under phenomenological noise. Each statistical certificate bounds the failure probability of an auxiliary decoder that divides the code into blocks and corrects each block using a window around it; optimal decoding does at least as well, so the bound also holds for optimal decoding. A deterministic lemma shows that the auxiliary decoder fails only if bad blocks, in which the window corrections leave a defect or a long residual path, form a sparse hierarchy that joins the two rough boundaries. This gives an explicit bound once every block is bad with probability below a limit, about $4\times10^{-4}$ under bit flips, and a pre-registered Monte Carlo experiment bounds these probabilities. The confidence rests on a binomial model of the counts of bad blocks and on two tested properties of each decoding program. All these results are proved in the proof assistant Lean 4, the statistical ones with the binomial model and the two properties as hypotheses.

papers.title: Classification of fixed points of the centroid body operator
papers.abstract: We classify the fixed points, up to dilation, of the classical volume-normalized centroid body operator in every dimension. We prove that ΓK = cK holds precisely for ellipsoids centered at the origin. The proof combines a signed spherical moment-gap argument in low dimensions with boundary integral operators, compact-group structure, and quantitative regression estimates in higher dimensions. Affine eigenfunctions force a large rotation subspace; curvature and log-concave regression bounds then exclude every proper such subspace. The remaining finite comparisons are certified by exact rational inequalities. The manuscript supplies proofs of the auxiliary analytic estimates and explicitly identifies the external results used.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 10: The Caceres Prime Function. A square-root damped prime weight, its exact Prime Zeta structure, and a dual spectrum of the Riemann zeros
papers.abstract: \sloppy We study the \emph{Caceres Prime Function} \[ \C(s)=\sum_{n\ge 2}\frac{a(n)}{n^{s}},\qquad a(n)=\sum_{p^k\,\|\,n}\frac{\log p}{\sqrt{p^{k}}}, \] the Dirichlet series of the additive function that weights each prime factor $p$ of $n$ by $\log p$ divided by the square root of the exact power of $p$ dividing $n$. \emph{Structure.} We prove that $\C=\zeta\K$, where the \emph{prime kernel}, $\K(s)=\sum_p\log p\,(1-p^{-s})/(p^{s+1/2}-1)$, is an exact telescoping series of shifted derivatives of the Prime Zeta function. So $\K$ is meromorphic in $\Re s>-\frac14$, and the line $\Re s=-\frac14$ is a natural boundary. Every zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ produces two singular points of $\K$, at $i\gamma$ and $i\gamma/2$, which are poles unless $2\gamma$ is again an ordinate with twice the multiplicity (respectively $\gamma/2$ an ordinate with half the multiplicity, for $i\gamma/2$); the exponent $\frac12$ is the normalization that puts both families on the imaginary axis. More precisely, $\K(s)=-\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(s+\frac12)+\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(2s+\frac12)-\frac1{12s}+H(s)$, with $H$ holomorphic in a neighbourhood of $\Re s\ge0$. \emph{RH criteria.} RH is equivalent to the holomorphy of $\K(s)-\frac1{s-1/2}+\frac1{2(s-1/4)}$ in $\Re s>0$. It is also equivalent to a bound $O(x^\varepsilon)$, or even a one-sided bound, for the remainder $R_b$ of the kernel's partial sums. Both are exact reformulations of RH, not proofs. \emph{Mean value and explicit formula.} Unconditionally, $\sum_{n\le x}a(n)=\K(1)x+2\zeta(\frac12)\sqrt x+O(\sqrt x\,e^{-c_\ast\sqrt{\log x}})$, with the explicit bound $5.51\sqrt x$ for the error after the first term when $x\ge10^6$. Under RH, the Riesz mean of $a$ has an explicit formula in which every zero contributes the pure phases $x^{i\gamma}$ and $x^{i\gamma/2}$ at constant amplitude. \emph{The Ces\`aro margin.} The kernel is Suzuki's one-variable margin $M$ seen at two scales. Unconditionally, $R_b(x)=\alpha(x)-\alpha(\sqrt x)+o(1)$, where $\alpha$ is the slope of the margin. Under RH, the kernel's Riesz margin is $M(N)-2M(\sqrt N)$. Its fluctuation has energy $2(\log\xi)''(\frac12)$, reduced by $2\gamma^{-2}$ for every pair of ordinates with $\gamma'=2\gamma$; the near pair $\gamma_{14}\approx2\gamma_4$ is visible in the data. \emph{Zeros of $\C$.} A computer-assisted proof shows that $\C$ has a zero near $1.379+8.639\,i$, in the half-plane of absolute convergence, and Bohr's theory gives $\gg T$ such zeros up to height $T$. So $\C$ is not an $L$-function. The theorems are proved here, except that Section~\ref{sec:margin} uses the formula for the margin and the almost periodicity of the slope from Part~11. Uncertified computations are labelled as numerical observations.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 16: How many positive directions does the Archimedean place have? A counting law with a boundary phase
papers.abstract: Restrict the archimedean part of Weil's quadratic form, for $\zeta$ or for a primitive real Dirichlet $L$-function of conductor $q$ and parity $\kappa$, to test functions supported in an interval of length $a$, and let $n_+(a)$ be the number of its positive directions, the directions that the pole and the primes must absorb. A Szeg\H{o}-type argument gives $n_+(a)=t_0a/\pi+o(a)$, where $t_0$ is the zero of $\vartheta'$. We observe that the form is $\Lambda-\psi_\kappa(-\Delta)$ with $\psi_\kappa$ a complete Bernstein function (proved) and, using the boundary phase of Kaleta, Kwa\'snicki and Ma{\l}ecki, we state, as a conjecture, the asymptotic law \[ n_+(a)=\Big\lfloor\frac{t_0a}\pi+\frac{2\varpi_\kappa(t_0)}\pi\Big\rfloor , \] with an explicit phase $\varpi_\kappa$ that depends only on the parity, the conductor entering only through $t_0$. We test it in seven cases, $\zeta$ and $\chi_{-3},\chi_{-4},\chi_5,\chi_{-7},\chi_8,\chi_{-8}$. On the finest mesh the shifts of the jumps $m=2,\dots,12$ bracket the prediction $2\varpi_\kappa(t_0)/\pi$, which ranges from $0.18$ to $0.59$, to within $1$ to $3\cdot10^{-3}$ for the characters and $3\cdot10^{-2}$ for $\zeta$. A second, independent implementation extrapolates in the mesh on three to nine jumps per case; the extrapolated shifts lie above the prediction by $0.2$ to $2.3\cdot10^{-4}$ in every case, a one-sided offset of the size of the extrapolation error, which we have checked to be a bias in one case only. The first jump is an exception, and for $\zeta$ the shift reaches its limit only after about ten jumps. A smoothed count removes the integer part and leaves ``degree plus constant'' with the boundary phase as constant; on a circle the constant is carried by the end points and cancels between an arc and its complement; and treating $-\log q$ as a degree, $q\leftrightarrow1/q$ acts on the band edge as $t_0\mapsto4\pi^2/t_0$ to leading order, with $\zeta$ at the self-dual point $t_0\approx2\pi$. We record what the law implies for the signature of Weil's form and where it stands with respect to the Riemann--Roch formulas for $\overline{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}$. The law is a conjecture supported by these computations. The Bernstein structure is proved here; the first-order count is quoted from Part~14 and its proof is not repeated.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 37: The $6k\pm1$ race: sieve structure, Chebyshev's bias and a GRH-equivalent inequality
papers.abstract: Every prime $p>3$ is $6k+1$ or $6k-1$. We collect what can be proved about the two resulting sequences and add three results. The races are those modulo $3$ (the prime $2$ counts for the class $2$); the race modulo $6$ differs by that one prime. (i) In the weighting $n^{-1/2}\log(N/n)$ of the Ces\`aro margin, the race between the prime powers $\equiv2$ and $\equiv1\pmod3$ is an exact identity. The $6k-1$ side leads by $2\frac{L'}L(\frac12,\chi_{-3})\log N-\frac12\psi'(\frac34)=1.1320\log N-1.2709$ plus the margin $M_\chi(N)$ of $L(s,\chi_{-3})$. The generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for $L(s,\chi_{-3})$ is equivalent to $M_\chi\ge0$ for all large $N$, and under GRH the weighted race is never lost after $N=2$. This is a criterion of the type of Hardy--Littlewood and Landau (1918) for Chebyshev's assertion, here with the Ces\`aro weight and with explicit constants. (ii) We verify $0.1024\le M_\chi(N)\le0.3549$ for $2\le N\le2^{27}$, inside the window $[0,0.4536]$ that GRH predicts. We also check the formula against the first $271$ zeros of $L(s,\chi_{-3})$. (iii) For the unweighted race, the bias is $1/\sqrt{V_\chi}=2.97$ standard deviations, with $V_\chi=\sum_\rho\frac1{\rho(1-\rho)}=0.113230$ (equal to $\sum_\rho|\rho|^{-2}$ under GRH); under GRH and linear independence, a recomputation with $271$ zeros gives the density $0.99906$, in agreement with the $0.9990$ of Rubinstein and Sarnak. Along the way we prove the sieve characterization of $6k\pm1$ and of twin primes, explain why Legendre-type counting cannot give the error term, compare twin primes and Goldbach representations modulo $6$ with the Hardy--Littlewood predictions, and prove the formula for $\gcd_p(p^{2n}-1)$ (the sequence $24,240,504,480,\dots$). Version~2 adds the generating function $\frac12[\zeta_6(s)^2\pm L(s,\chi_6)^2]$ of the three forms $6xy\pm x\pm y$, and a duality theorem: averaged over the zeros of $\zeta$, the cross-energy $\mathcal C_2(N,\frac12,\gamma)$ of Part~1 returns $\log N/N$; averaged over the zeros of $L(s,\chi_{-3})$ it returns $\frac1N\sum_{d\mid N}\chi_{-3}(d)\Lambda(d)$; and M\"obius inversion separates the primes of the two lanes. Version~3 makes this exact at finite height and without RH: with a Gaussian weight on the zeros, the cross-energy satisfies an explicit formula whose pole term is $\mathcal C_2$ itself at $s=0$, whose prime term is $\log N$ exactly plus a nonnegative remainder from the near coincidences $nj\approx N$, and which returns every prime power up to $60$ from the $1517$ zeros below $2000$. Nothing here proves RH, GRH, or the twin prime or Goldbach conjectures.

papers.title: Cross-Energy of Dirichlet Partial Sums. Part 38: The energy of the Chebyshev race: an explicit unconditional floor for the prime race between the lanes $6k\pm1$
papers.abstract: Let $R(x)=\pi(x;3,2)-\pi(x;3,1)$ be the Chebyshev race between the two prime lanes $6k\mp1$ (the prime $2$ counted, by the congruence $2\equiv-1$ mod $3$, in the $6k-1$ lane). We study the race as an \emph{energy} and establish three things (the energy law uses two estimates imported from the $\zeta$ case; see Proposition~\ref{prop:cramer}). First, an elementary ledger identity: the entire bias of the race is the bookkeeping of prime squares, which all land in the lane $6k+1$; subtracting the ledger $\tfrac12\pi(\sqrt x)$ turns a walk with \emph{zero} sign changes up to $10^8$ into one with $15{,}329$ ($21{,}329$ if every passage between $D>0$ and $D\le0$ at a prime is counted). Second, the mean energy of the normalized race signal $e(u)=e^{-u/2}\psi(e^u,\chi_3)$ admits an explicit unconditional lower bound for its upper limit, which we call the floor, \[ \limsup_{U\to\infty}\frac1U\int_0^U e(u)^2\,du\;\ge\;\kappa_3 :=\sum_{\rho}\frac{1}{\rho(1-\rho)} =\log\frac3\pi-\gamma_E+2\,\frac{L'}{L}(1,\chi_3) =0.113229969857\ldots, \] the sum running over the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_3)$ with multiplicity, and the limit exists and attains the floor if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds for $L(s,\chi_3)$ with all zeros simple. The constant is known: under GRH it is the variance of the limiting distribution of Rubinstein and Sarnak for $(\log x/\sqrt x)R(x)$ (four times smaller than in their normalization $E(x;3,2)-E(x;3,1)$), and its closed form is that of Fiorilli and Martin (there under GRH); it is also the variance $V_\chi$ of Part~37, on the $6k\pm1$ race, where the prime-square mechanism of the bias is identified; what is added here is the unconditional floor with its equality case and exponential-growth law, the ledger correction of the counting race, and the exact measurement. The constant $\kappa_3$ is the exact analogue, for the prime race, of the B\'aez-Duarte constant $2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi$ of the Nyman--Beurling criterion. Third, we measure: from all prime powers up to $10^8$, by exact piecewise integration, the cumulative mean energy is $0.1201$ at $x=10^8$ and lies $4$ to $12\%$ above $\kappa_3$ for $10^4\le x\le10^8$. This is consistent with the theorem and does not test it: the floor is a statement about an upper limit, obtained from the dichotomy between GRH and its failure, and means over single decades fall below $\kappa_3$ ($0.102$ on $[10^4,10^5]$, $0.113$ on $[10^7,10^8]$). The second-order term is $(\text{mean}-\kappa_3)\cdot U\approx0.11$ (between $0.09$ and $0.13$), the race analogue of the second-order constant $K=2.5124797\ldots$ of the prime energy. The proofs of the energy law transplant the $C_2$ energy law for $\zeta$ to $L(s,\chi_3)$, where the absence of a pole simplifies every step.

papers.title: Divisors of Mersenne numbers under doubling
papers.abstract: This paper studies a question of Erdős about how the total number of divisors of Mersenne numbers grows when the range is doubled. We prove that the doubling ratio is always at least 3, sharp, and nearly 4 whenever the relevant Fermat numbers are composite, as all known ones are. We also reduce the open question of whether the ratio tends to infinity to a statement about indices with few divisors. This leads to a new conjecture on the prime factors of Mersenne numbers next to near-Wagstaff numbers, which we study through implications, barrier results and a proven polynomial analogue.

papers.title: Domino insertion and cells in type B
papers.abstract: We prove Conjectures A, A$^{+}$, and B of Bonnafé, Geck, Iancu, and Lam on Kazhdan–Lusztig cells in type $B$.

papers.title: Euler's 1747 conjecture on sums of integers with restricted prime factors
papers.abstract: We prove that every positive integer congruent to $2$ modulo $4$ is a sum of two positive integers whose prime factors are all congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, with $1$ admitted as a summand. Euler proposed this statement in a letter to Goldbach dated May 6, 1747. The proof counts representations by four squares and bounds those containing a common prime divisor congruent to $3$ modulo $4$ in either coordinate pair. An average over a nonsplit torus normalizer converts the quaternionic Hecke bound into an error independent of the sieving prime. Elementary estimates then give the explicit threshold $64^4$. An exact finite arithmetic certificate covers the remaining $4{,}194{,}304$ integers in the required residue class.

papers.title: Exact projector-rank thresholds for state-independent contextuality
papers.abstract: For every integer r ≥ 1 we construct a finite exclusivity graph Fr with the following two properties. First, Fr has a projective representation by pairwise distinct projectors of rank r that exhibits state-independent contextuality. Second, no projective representation of Fr by projectors of any common rank s < r, in any finite dimension, exhibits state-independent contextuality; in every such representation the maximally mixed state is noncontextual. This establishes, for every r, the “rank efficient” scenarios sought by Hohn, Xu and Kleinmann, for which only numerical evidence at r = 2, 3 was available. The graph is the disjunctive product of an odd cycle C2r+1 with the orthogonality structure of a rank-one contextuality set whose fractional chromatic number exceeds its dimension by an arbitrarily small amount. Such sets are obtained from the infinite family of Kochen–Specker parity proofs in R^4 of Elford and Lisonek, together with a coning construction that raises the dimension by one.

papers.title: Exact sizes of networks that select the three or four largest of n elements
papers.abstract: We study $(t,n)$-selection networks, which move the $t$ largest of $n$ inputs to $t$ given lines in any order, and the least number $\hat U_t(n)$ of comparators in such a network. Alekseev showed that $\hat U_t(n)\ge(n-t)\lceil\lg(t+1)\rceil$. For $t=2^k\ge 4$ we raise this bound by $k-1$ for every $n>t$, and by $2k-5$ when $t\ge 32$; as far as we know, these are the first improvements at powers of two. The proofs follow the weights of the lines, and a pruning step of Yao extends the gain to every $t\ge 3$. For $t=3$, Yao's upper bound $2n-5+\lfloor\lg(n-3)\rfloor$ is exact for $4\le n\le 18$. For $t=4$ the new bound is $3n-11$ for all $n\ge 5$, and the value $3n-10$ that Knuth expected is exact for $6\le n\le 12$. Their lower bounds rest on exhaustive searches at a few sizes and on the fact that one more input costs at least two more comparators. Most of the results are also proved in Lean 4, some through compiled checks.

papers.title: Explicit bounds for odd perfect and quasiperfect numbers
papers.abstract: Let $N$ be an odd perfect number or a quasiperfect number, and let $B(N) = \prod_{p \mid N} (1+1/p)$. We prove that $2 < N/\varphi(N) < 2.17372$ and that $105 \nmid N$, and we obtain explicit two-sided bounds for $B(N)$ according to the value of $\gcd(15,N)$. For an odd perfect number $N$, they give $B(N) > 1.90281$, $1.70584$, $1.83233$ and $1.67856$ when $\gcd(15,N) = 1$, $3$, $5$ and $15$, respectively, and $B(N) < 1.84348$, $1.93549$ and $1.84125$ when $\gcd(15,N) = 3$, $5$ and $15$. These follow from general bounds for $B(n)$ in terms of $n/\varphi(n)$, of the abundancy index $I(n) = \sigma(n)/n$, and of $\sum_{p \mid n} 1/p$. We also bound the abundancy indices of $N \operatorname{rad}(N)$ and $N/\operatorname{rad}(N)$ and the functions $\sigma^{\pm}$, $\varphi^{+}$ and $\psi^{+}$ of S\'andor and Atanassov at $N$, give an explicit lower bound for the number of distinct prime factors of $N$ in terms of its least prime factor, and show that the sum of the reciprocals of the prime factors of a quasiperfect number $N$ is less than $\log I(N)$. Finally, for the shifted abundancy indices $I^{+}(n) = 1 + \sum_{d \mid n, \, d > 1} 1/(d+1)$ and $I^{-}(n) = 1 + \sum_{d \mid n, \, d > 1} 1/(d-1)$, we determine the optimal constants in the comparisons of $I^{+}$, $I$ and $I^{-}$ on the odd integers and on the odd integers with at most one odd exponent, and we deduce $1.8471 < I^{+}(N) < 2 < I^{-}(N) < 2.2722$ and $I^{-}(N) - I^{+}(N) < 0.42493$ for every odd perfect number $N$.

papers.title: Explicit Weak abc Inequalities and the Discrete Obstruction to Full abc in the DIC Framework
papers.abstract: Independent audit and coefficient verification of C. Soulé's preprint "On the abc conjecture" (arXiv:2611.05217, 2026). This work neither proves nor disproves the abc conjecture; all No-Go statements are internal to the audited construction, and every statement that uses Soulé's Theorem A is explicitly tagged as conditional on it. We axiomatise the DIC framework and prove three stratified groups of results on Kodaira--Parshin arithmetic surface fibrations. (i) Unconditional geometric theorems: the adjunction identity $Z\cdot\omega_{\mathcal{X}/B}=-Z^{2}$, the Riemann--Hurwitz intersection numbers, the invariants of the general $(g_0,r,b)$ construction, and a Deligne--Riemann--Roch decomposition $c=\frac{2b^{2}+2b-1}{12}+(D_0-T)/\omega^{2}$ of the arithmetic coefficient. (ii) A meta-theorem: integrality of torsion lengths forces the coefficient of Theorem A onto the discrete set $t=12/N$, $N\equiv 1\pmod 3$ (at the literature point $(q,\lambda)=(5,3)$; for varying $q$ this is an arithmetic coincidence, not a structural barrier). A local hyperelliptic model gives $T=8k$, $t=12$ as the unique transverse output; second-order torsion gives $n_1=n_2$, hence $\Theta=T/k\in 2\mathbb{Z}$, leaving $(\Theta,q)=(12,27)$ as the sole lattice candidate. The unified criterion $E=12(q-1)/(qN\gamma)$ has the unique solution $(N,\Theta,q,\gamma)=(13,12,27,8/9)$; the height is the canonical-bundle height of a fixed genus-$2$ curve ($\gamma=2/5$, confirmed by $12/\gamma=30$ in the source), so $(12,27)$ requires genus $13$ and lies outside the theorem's hypotheses: the last cell is empty. (iii) Controlled weak abc: all unconditional bounds known for abc are of exponential type ($\log c\ll N^{1/3}(\log N)^{3}$; Stewart--Yu); the exponent below is of polynomial type, and its existence is what Theorem A supplies. We derive $\eta(q)=(q-1)/q$, unify the exponent as $E=t\eta/\gamma$, and obtain $E_{\max}=12\frac{q-1}{q}\bigl\lceil\frac{2q-2}{\ell}\bigr\rceil$. A discriminant stratification sharpens this to $c\le A_{\varepsilon}(N/M_5)^{24+\varepsilon}$; bootstrapping to exponent $1$ is impossible ($\inf\theta=0$); the discriminant-to-degree ratio is tower-monotone; $4/5$ is an Artin conductor identity; and the isometry step (32) of the source contributes only $O(d')$, derived unconditionally from a finite Čech complex, leaving $\frac32=m\cdot c$, $36$, $12$, $24$ and $E(c)=12/(5-18c)$ unchanged. A verbatim check of the source confirms twelve items, including the statement and scope of Theorem A; the constant $12$ decomposes as $\frac13\cdot\frac{m}{\rho-mc}$; and Route 1 is closed. Full abc is unattainable inside the audited construction for nine independent reasons, none depending on the truth of Theorem A: hypothesis exclusion, $\inf\theta=0$, tower monotonicity, bridge breaking, the $S$-smoothness loop, the double exclusion $T/k=47/3$, the $g_0=13$ collapse, index-ideal absorption with exact slope $2/(n-1)$, and the distributional vanishing of the discount (the multiplicity excess and $\theta$ have density $1-o(1)$, with explicit large-deviation rates).

papers.title: Expressiveness, Verifiability, Tractability: Toward a Computational Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: An investigation into the existence of a conservation law governing computational behaviour, in the form of the Expressiveness, Verifiability, Tractability (EVT) Hypothesis, is undertaken. The hypothesis is motivated by a simple observation: mechanisms that increase what a system can directly express, powerful control, effects, reflection, meta-programming, and self-interpretation, tend to undermine what can be verified uniformly and mechanically, while regimes that maximize static guarantees typically do so by restricting expressiveness or relocating effort into compilers, proof artifacts, or human interpretation. We analyze canonical failure modes that arise when one attempts to push beyond this frontier, distinguishing collapse of correctness, collapse of compilability, and collapse of comprehensibility. We then develop an order-theoretic model for comparing languages and verification disciplines and define an “E/V boundary” as a Pareto frontier in a partially ordered design space. Finally, we sketch how analogous tradeoffs appear in other computational domains, suggesting that “thermodynamic” boundary behaviour may be a recurring feature of expressive formalisms that demand strong global guarantees and within physical methods of information processing.

papers.title: Finite-length permutation modules for\\free-amalgamation structures of arbitrary arity
papers.abstract: Let $\A$ be the countable homogeneous limit of a free-amalgamation class in a finite relational language, expanded by a generic linear order. We prove that its tuple permutation modules have finite composition length over every field, also after naming finitely many points. More precisely, each orbit of increasing $d$-tuples disjoint from the named points has a permutation module of length $2^d$. This extends the theorem of Yang--Boja\'nczyk--Klin from unary and binary relations to relations of arbitrary arity. The main step shows that every finitely supported array whose sums over each single coordinate vanish is a linear combination of alternating sums obtained by independently doubling its coordinates. Its proof combines a Ramsey separation theorem with a construction that moves finite configurations into prescribed order intervals. Over a finite field, we also obtain finitely many closed invariant linear subspaces of $\F^{A^k}$; each is generated, in the product topology, by functions definable using at most $k$ additional parameters.

papers.title: Finite-preparation response under heavy-tailed catastrophes: exact amplitudes and separation from Poisson coverage
papers.abstract: We determine the terminal response of a one-dimensional binary recovery process to a finite preparation history under independently renewed Poisson interval catastrophes. For regularly varying interval weights $\nu_r\sim r^{-p}L(r)$, $p>3$, and fixed small positive intensities, we prove an exact leading response when preparation and observation durations grow proportionally. The main result expresses the response as an explicit functional of the actual recovery-front speeds accumulated along each fixed finite-stage preparation history and of the selected target-phase open density. Its weak-intensity second variation is a strictly positive quadratic form in every nonzero fixed signed temporal modulation, including equal-dose redistributions. A separate four-update theorem identifies local cooperation through an explicit positive equal-dose contrast for every nonzero interval law with finite first moment. These positive contrasts separate the process from conditional Poisson Boolean coverage with fixed grain kernels, a fixed environment distribution and affine intensity control, whose contrast is nonpositive at every finite time. As an effective extension, relative power-law tail bounds yield a conservative computable sufficient threshold valid at every later integer time. The core proof combines nonstationary front transfer, uniform background forgetting and exact resetting at intensity switches.

papers.title: Fixed points of the polar projection body operator and its square
papers.abstract: Let $TK=(\Pi K)^\circ$ be the polar projection body of a convex body $K$ in $\R^n$. In dimension $n\ge3$, we prove that $TK$ is a positive dilate of $K$ exactly when $K$ is an origin-centred ellipsoid, settling Petty's polar projection conjecture. The same classification holds under the weaker assumption that $T^2K$ is a positive dilate of $K$. The proof uses a distributional Laplacian identity to compare two integrals of central section volumes. Equality supplies contractive hyperplane projections with every kernel direction, and James's theorem gives ellipsoidal rigidity. The argument applies to arbitrary convex bodies and yields the translative constant volume conjecture of Horv\'ath and L\'angi.

papers.title: Formal Verification of a Computer-Assisted Proof in Celestial Mechanics
papers.abstract: Albouy, Fu and Sun conjectured in 2008 that four positive masses admit, for each cyclic order of the bodies, exactly one convex central configuration up to similarity; the question is Problem 10 of a 2012 list of open problems on the $n$-body problem. We recently proved the conjecture by reducing it to an inequality for a trace at the real zeros of an equation in four variables; a branch and bound that starts from a grid of 136,448 boxes establishes the inequality. In this paper we describe a formalization of the whole proof in Lean 4 and Mathlib in which Lean's kernel checks the computation, using decide +kernel, so that no compiler has to be trusted. Our checker stores an interval as two natural numbers in a biased fixed-point format. The kernel can then hand all the arithmetic to GMP. Functions are enclosed over boxes by first-order slopes. An unverified search records the decisions for each box in one natural number, and the checker replays them. We write each formula once over a type class; evaluating it at a type that pairs a real number with an interval then proves the enclosure correct. Checking the 3418 certificate theorems takes 7.6 hours of processor time, and the independent type checker nanoda accepts the proof. A version rebuilt on one eighth of the boxes passed three type checkers in 2.9 hours on a public registry of formal proofs.

papers.title: Genuinely multipartite bound entanglement of three qubits
papers.abstract: If a three-party state is positive under partial transposition (PPT) across each of its three bipartitions, no local protocol can distil any pure entanglement from it: neither singlets between any two parties nor GHZ states. All of its entanglement is bound. We show that such a state can nevertheless be genuinely multipartite entangled (GME), meaning that it cannot be prepared by mixing states in each of which some party is unentangled from the rest. This already happens for three qubits, the smallest system in which the question arises and a common experimental setting for multipartite entanglement; to our knowledge no three-qubit example was known. An explicit mixture of five orthogonal states (one GHZ-type, three $W$-type and one product state) is PPT across every cut and GME throughout an exact parameter interval, and its rank, five, is the minimum possible. Genuine entanglement is proved by a witness acting only on the five-dimensional support, whose nonnegativity on the biseparable states in that support reduces to a sum of squares on its curves of product vectors. Such states are invisible to the PPT-mixture test, the standard semidefinite relaxation used to certify GME, yet they form a set with nonempty interior among density matrices: an explicit full-rank example remains GME under $2.33\%$ white noise, while $2.336\%$ makes it biseparable. We also construct extreme examples with the smallest possible partial-transpose ranks $(5,5,5,5)$. All our explicit states, including the full-rank one, lie in the mixed $W$ class: they are mixtures of pure states with vanishing three-tangle, so their genuine entanglement needs no GHZ-type component. Full PPT therefore does not imply biseparability, even for three qubits.

papers.title: Irrational even beta values from powered hypergeometric kernels
papers.abstract: For the Dirichlet beta function, we prove that at least one of $\beta(6),\beta(8),\ldots,\beta(74)$ is irrational, and that at least one of $\beta(8),\beta(10),\ldots,\beta(110)$ is irrational. These shorten the previously stated intervals with the same starting indices, whose upper endpoints are $92$ and $128$, respectively (twinheterodox, Hexagon 2611.00160v2, Section 8.2). The new bounds come from a different construction, based on powers of Krisman's hypergeometric kernel (Hexagon 2610.00285v2).

papers.title: Joint distribution of factorial units and valuations in translated intervals
papers.abstract: For every fixed finite set of primes, the corresponding prime valuations of factorials, reduced modulo arbitrary fixed integers, and the prime-free parts, reduced modulo arbitrary fixed prime powers, have a joint uniform distribution. We give a proof with a power-saving error on every interval of consecutive nonnegative integers, uniform in the interval's starting point. A fixed congruence on the index may be imposed independently. The resulting statement for the part of a factorial coprime to an arbitrary fixed modulus gives the densities and relative density asked for in Problems 2 and 3 of Hajdu and Papp. The proof uses a finite digit-window identity, a strict local character contraction, and a carry estimate followed by finite Fourier analysis.

papers.title: Laurent Phenomenon Algebras on Minuscule Grassmannians and their Mirrors
papers.abstract: We construct Laurent phenomenon algebra structures on the homogeneous coordinate rings of the half-spin Grassmannians and the Freudenthal variety. Their frozen variables are the linear coordinates in a Coxeter orbit, and the resulting boundary divisors are anticanonical. Together with the construction of Daisey--Ducat for the Cayley plane, these examples admit explicit mirrors described by Newton polytopes. We identify the upper Laurent phenomenon algebras of the mirror seeds with the intrinsic mirror algebras of Keel--Yu at the specialization $q^\beta=1$, including the theta functions associated with the individual boundary components. The half-spin construction is uniform in the rank. In the exceptional cases, contact calculations and Laurent divisibility determine the local expansions; the Freudenthal comparison also uses exact calculations of divisorial valuations. We obtain integral comparisons and valuative independence of the intrinsic theta basis in every reachable seed.

papers.title: Limit Cycles under Concave Per-Capita Growth
papers.abstract: We study predator--prey systems with a fixed globally linear functional response and a strictly concave prey per-capita growth rate. For every $N\ge1$ and $K\ge2$, we construct a growth polynomial of degree $2N+2\lceil K/2\rceil+2$ with exactly $N$ positive periodic orbits, all hyperbolic. The construction retains a chosen center $K$-jet and the low-density growth rate and carrying capacity of its limiting profile, subject to an explicit relation between the center height and curvature. A limiting Lyapunov function and return-map estimates at three amplitude scales exclude additional cycles. A dissipative extension gives exact global counts with prescribed limiting center energies. We also prove that profiles with at least $N$ hyperbolic cycles are $C^2$-dense in the admissible class, while preserving the entire germ at the maximum and both ecological endpoint values. The first nonzero canonical odd term determines the sharp differentiability threshold. Further results give parity restrictions for fixed focus jets, degree lower bounds, quantitative polynomial approximation under concavity and interpolation constraints, and amplitude and multiplicity interpolation by Abelian integrals. Finally, a single smooth strictly concave profile has infinitely many nested hyperbolic cycles converging to coexistence.

papers.title: Local optimality of rank-47 schemes for 4×4 matrix multiplication over F2
papers.abstract: The tensor $\langle 4,4,4\rangle$ of $4\times4$ matrix multiplication has rank at most 47 over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and as it is not known whether 47 is optimal, we ask how far the known decompositions of rank 47 are from one of rank 46. A decomposition is locally optimal to depth $D$ if no $D$ or fewer of its rank-one terms can be replaced by fewer rank-one terms. We prove that five pairwise inequivalent decompositions of rank 47 over $\mathbb{F}_2$ are locally optimal to depth 18, as is every decomposition equivalent to one of them, so a decomposition of rank 46 over $\mathbb{F}_2$ shares at most 28 terms with any decomposition in these five classes. The five classes include the scheme of Fawzi et al. and every public decomposition of rank 47 over $\mathbb{F}_2$ known to us; one of them, found in our flip-graph searches, is new. The proof rests on a peeling lemma and, for four sets of terms that resist the other bounds, on a refinement of the substitution method, which we call substitution over subspaces with lifting. Local optimality to depth 18 is also proved in Lean 4.

papers.title: Lower bounds for the Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley constant
papers.abstract: Let $\beta$ be the Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley constant: the shortest tour through $n$ independent uniform random points in the unit square has length asymptotic to $\beta\sqrt n$ almost surely. Dong and Cao proved $\beta\ge0.6421$ from an inequality $\beta\ge5/8+\sum_{k=3}^{K}C_k$, where $C_k$ is an integral over configurations of $k$ points in the plane that form a connected graph when points at distance at most $1$ are joined. For $C_3$, $C_4$ and $C_5$, sharper bounds come from a first-order expansion of the area of the union of the unit disks on boxes of configurations. For $C_6+\dots+C_{22}$, which Dong and Cao did not use, a lower bound comes from comparing each point only with the three points before it in the order of their first coordinates. We obtain $\beta\ge0.6496$, and $\beta\ge0.6508$ if the exponential function of the C library used to evaluate the bound for $C_6+\dots+C_{22}$ has a relative error below $10^{-9}$. The proofs are computer-assisted; the bound $0.6496$ is proved in Lean 4, with finite checks evaluated by compiled code, from the inequality of Dong and Cao and two statements about unions of disks that we prove but do not formalize.

papers.title: Lusztig's Fourier matrix conjecture for finite noncrystallographic Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof of Lusztig's Fourier matrix conjecture for all finite noncrystallographic Coxeter groups. For every two-sided cell, the normalized \(S\)-matrix of the Drinfeld center of its asymptotic Hecke category, equipped with the inherited pivotal structure, equals the corresponding Fourier matrix in the modular convention. In particular, we establish the exact \(74\times74\) matrix identity for the middle cell of type \(H_4\).

papers.title: Marked-point modules and central nilpotents at roots of unity
papers.abstract: We study extensions in the two-marked-point representation of the periodic Temperley--Lieb algebra at $q=e^{i\pi/p}$, $p\in\mathbb Z_{\geq3}$. For every positive even size $N$, we construct a submodule $Z_N$ extending $T_N=W_{N;2,\varepsilon}$ by $W_N=W_{N;0,\varepsilon q}$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$. The dual trees of noncrossing matchings give an explicit injection $\Theta_N:T_N\to W_N$. Both central braid transfer elements have nilpotent part $g\Theta_N\pi_N$ on $Z_N$, where $\pi_N$ is the quotient map and $g=x+x^{-1}+\varepsilon(y+y^{-1})$ for the marked-point parameters $x,y\in\mathbb{C}^\times$. The extension splits exactly when $g=0$, and the formula determines the central Jordan forms at every even size. In the window $2\leq N<2p-2$, $Z_N$ is a joint central summand and, when $g\ne0$, has simple layers $T_N/S_N/T_N$. An explicit intertwiner and annular localization identify its two-layer quotient with a periodic XXZ sector. The associated basic image algebras have dimensions five and four; the quotient preserves first extensions between simples and kills a nonzero Yoneda product in degree two. An annular operator detects the extension with coefficient $2\varepsilon g$. Beyond the isolated window, we determine a five-simple image algebra and compute a $43$-dimensional joint central summand at $p=3,N=6$, on which the two central nilpotents generate a four-dimensional algebra. Exact matrix calculations and verification code accompany these finite computations.

papers.title: Nonstabilization of the Predictive Boolean Lookahead Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We study the hierarchy of languages generated by predictive Boolean $\mathrm{LL}(k)$ grammars. The model uses a deterministic recursive-descent table, strongly non-left-recursive rules, and at least one positive conjunct per rule. For every integer $r\geq1$, we construct a language over a fixed eight-letter alphabet that has an ordinary $\mathrm{LL}(r+r2^r+2)$ grammar and establish that it has no predictive Boolean $\mathrm{LL}(r)$ grammar. The construction asks for a specified token in a uniquely decodable word. The lower bound represents parsing on a long unary prefix by finitely many forward-moving endpoint streams and a finite Boolean recurrence. Random binary blocks followed by homogeneous blocks separate streams with a persistent timing error from streams having an exact finite-state potential. A bounded-lookahead argument hides a token-count change from each remaining stream. An encoding of the resulting independent queries is then shorter than their arbitrary binary payload. This gives nonstabilization under the stated predictive convention. The conclusion is for the stated parser model, including positive-conjunct and strong non-left-recursion requirements. Path-dependent tables satisfying these requirements give the same language families.

papers.title: On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in the octonionic projective plane
papers.abstract: Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a four-parameter family of tight $39$-point codes in the octonionic projective plane. We show that near each member outside a closed nowhere-dense set of resonant parameters, the labeled tight codes modulo $F_4$ form exactly four ten-dimensional families, any two meeting in the four-parameter family, although the first-order deformations of the member form a $28$-dimensional space modulo $F_4$. The originally constructed code is resonant, and we do not determine the tight codes near it; but every neighborhood of it in the space of unlabeled tight $39$-point codes modulo $F_4$ contains a nonempty open subset homeomorphic to an open subset of $\mathbb R^{10}$, so any neighborhood of it that is a manifold has dimension ten.

papers.title: On the minimal dimension of range-criterion counterexamples to the PPT² conjecture
papers.abstract: The PPT$^2$ conjecture asserts that the composition of two completely positive and completely copositive (PPT) maps is entanglement breaking. A recently announced counterexample, with PPT maps $\mathrm{M}_{10}\to\mathrm{M}_6\to\mathrm{M}_{10}$, is certified by the range criterion: the range of the composite Choi matrix contains no nonzero product vector. We ask how small a counterexample certified in this way can be. For PPT maps $\Phi\colon\mathrm{M}_m\to\mathrm{M}_k$ and $\Psi\colon\mathrm{M}_k\to\mathrm{M}_n$ with $\Psi\circ\Phi\neq0$ and $\max(m,k,n)\le6$ we prove that the range of the Choi matrix of $\Psi\circ\Phi$ contains a nonzero product vector whenever $k\le5$ or $\min(m,n)\le5$. Hence the range criterion cannot certify a counterexample on $\mathrm{M}_4$ or $\mathrm{M}_5$, and among the types with all three dimensions at most six only $(6,6,6)$ remains open. Since the range is spanned by products of Kraus operators, the question is when such a span can avoid the matrices of rank one. The computer-assisted proof combines rank bounds for PPT maps with Chern class and excess intersection computations; its computed facts are checked in Lean 4, modulo classical, quoted or hand-proved inputs. The announced counterexample lifts through exterior powers a map on $\mathrm{M}_4$ built from a pencil of real matrices (a map of pencil type). When the map of pencil type loses rank transversally at finitely many points, its lifts through any Schur functor, exterior powers included, put product vectors into the kernel of the composite Choi matrix. When the composite is also nonzero, these product vectors form an unextendible product set only for exterior powers, and then one of the three dimensions is at least ten.

papers.title: On the structure of countable hyperspaces of regular subcontinua
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metric continuum and let $\mathcal D(X)$ be its hyperspace of regular subcontinua, that is, of the subcontinua of $X$ which are the closure of their interior. We prove that if $\mathcal D(X)$ is countable, then the interiors of its minimal elements are dense in $X$, and every regular subcontinuum is determined by the minimal elements it contains. We further establish that $\mathcal D(X)$ is a $G_\delta$ subset of the hyperspace $C(X)$ of subcontinua whenever $X$ admits a family of regular subcontinua whose interiors have dense union and which satisfies an absorption property. Consequently, every countable $\mathcal D(X)$ is completely metrizable and scattered. In particular, $\mathcal D(X)$ is never homeomorphic to the rational numbers, which answers a question of Ramírez Angarita and of Camargo, Ordoñez and Ramírez. The theorems of the paper are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Optimal Packing of Eleven Unit Squares: The Formalized Voronoi-Cell Proof
papers.abstract: We explain the computer-assisted proof that eleven independently rotated unit squares require a square container of side at least T = 3.8770835900228141773 . . ., the side attained by the known construction attributed to Walter Trump. The proof reduces arbitrary packings to 2,184 patterns of occupied closed Voronoi cells. Exact geometric certificates exclude 2,180 patterns, a square-symmetry argument reduces the remaining four to one, and a complete subdivision of that case places every possible smaller packing inside an explicitly certified isolation neighborhood. We give the geometric definitions, prove the continuous soundness rules underlying the finite calculations, and explain the common-cone local isolation argument used in the Lean development. The large certificate instances are identified by pinned source references; they are not replaced by numerical experiments. The reported formal verification uses Lean’s kernel together with its native compiler for specified numerical certificates.

papers.title: Osterwalder–Schrader axioms for scalar QED$_3$ in the Coulomb phase
papers.abstract: King constructed the continuum, infinite-volume limit of three-dimensional scalar quantum electrodynamics, the $U(1)$ (abelian) Higgs model, along Neumann–Dirichlet cubes. For his state at fixed photon mass we prove the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms: regularity $\mathrm{E0}''$ with absolute constants, invariance under the full Euclidean group, reflection positivity about every plane, symmetry, and the measure with its ergodic decomposition, on whose components the cluster axiom holds in all its forms. Rotation invariance is proved by comparing King's cubes with periodic tori carrying a smooth mass wall on two lattices whose orientations differ by $\arctan(3/4)$. With real scalar sources, the joint field of the curvature and the renormalised Wick square satisfies, on a tube of small Wick amplitudes, the axioms: regularity, invariance under translations and the lattice point group, Euclidean invariance of the joint field outside an exceptional set of couplings, reflection positivity for Wick amplitudes below a threshold, symmetry, and the measure with the cluster axiom in its weak form; above the threshold the Euclidean clause is open. The curvature results hold on King's whole coupling range; the Wick results hold under a one-sided sign clause of the Wick leg, which we prove on explicit coupling regions. The limit of vanishing photon mass is treated in a subsequent paper.

papers.title: Osterwalder–Schrader axioms for scalar QED$_3$ in the Higgs phase
papers.abstract: We study scalar quantum electrodynamics in three dimensions (QED$_3$) in its Higgs phase: the three-dimensional lattice abelian Higgs model in unitary gauge, with the Villain action, on lattices whose spacing tends to zero with canonically scaled couplings. At each spacing we construct infinite-volume states, as limit points of the periodic states and as limits of states in finite boxes; they carry the lattice symmetries, reflection positivity and bounds uniform in the volume. For the smeared curvature and bounded functions of the density, the generating functionals converge along a subsequence of spacings to a translation-invariant limit functional with the continuity required for the Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction. For the limits built on the box states, and on the periodic states along dyadic sequences of sides, the limit curvature field satisfies the axioms OS0–OS3, with invariance under the full Euclidean group. The cluster axiom OS4 is proved in a weak form, on almost every ergodic component. The tools are Gaussian domination of the Villain curvature, Ginibre inequalities and reflection positivity.

papers.title: Periodic counterexamples to three conjectures on Kolakoski transforms
papers.abstract: The simple Kolakoski transform need not preserve the limiting mean of a periodic word on $\{1,2\}$. We give a counterexample with input period $24$ and output period $12$, and a balanced counterexample whose input has mean $3/2$ while its output has mean $13/9$. Both examples remain unchanged under every realization of a nonconstant summable perturbation of the weights. Their discrepancies from the input means are linear. Consequently they contradict Conjectures (1), (2), and (4) of Cloitre. These statements concern auxiliary transforms of periodic inputs; the classical Kolakoski frequency problem remains open.

papers.title: Quadratic Strictly Positive Real Factors of Stable Transfer Functions
papers.abstract: We characterize factorizations \(G=G_0\circ H\) in which \(G\) and \(G_0\) are stable, minimum-phase, biproper real-rational functions with simple poles and zeros and positive gains at infinity, and \(H\) is a quadratic strictly positive real function. Classical rational decomposition identifies the quadratic right-factor classes with real Möbius involutions fixing \(G\). Within each class, we parameterize all normalized representatives and eliminate the scaling parameter and the frequency variable. The resulting sign conditions involve univariate polynomials of degree at most four. They determine all feasible denominator intervals and all factorizations in the class; for real-algebraic input, they give an exact decision procedure. We also give a scaling that maximizes the smaller of the inner positive-real margin and the outer spectral margin for a fixed denominator. For quadratic input, existence is equivalent to strict positive realness of \(G\) and to an explicit coefficient inequality. Examples exhibit a disconnected feasible parameter set, separate algebraic and analytic obstructions, and a quartic input with exactly three admissible classes.

papers.title: Re-proving native_decide facts in Lean's kernel: a study of 16 public packages and a converter
papers.abstract: Lean's native_decide proves a decidable proposition by running compiled code and records the result as an axiom. Mathlib forbids such axioms, and lake check and Comparator in Lean 4.35 reject them, as do the independent proof checkers. NativeTrust re-proves the recorded facts in Lean's kernel, with only the standard axioms and without editing the projects that contain them. Where a definition blocks kernel evaluation and NativeTrust has a version proved equal to it (for example, a fuel-indexed form of well-founded recursion), the converter evaluates a copy that uses that version. It then proves the copy equal to the original, usually by congruence. With its default settings it converts 98.2% of 52,821 native facts in 16 public packages. The three largest packages hold 94% of these facts; outside them it converts 68.5%. Nearly every converted fact needed nothing beyond plain kernel evaluation. Two tools remove the native axioms that the kernel can prove within a budget: a single import that makes each call of the tactic try the kernel first, and a source rewriter.

papers.title: Sharp Ionization Bounds for Helium and Lithium
papers.abstract: How many electrons can a nucleus bind? In the non-relativistic Coulomb model, Lieb proved in 1984 that a nucleus of charge $Z$ binds fewer than $2Z+1$ electrons. While this bound has been improved, the sharp upper bound has remained unknown for any nucleus other than hydrogen. We solve this problem for $Z=2$ and $Z=3$ by proving that helium binds two or fewer electrons and lithium binds four or fewer. Both bounds are sharp. Our main tool is an adaptation of Lieb's argument with a quadratic weight, which reduces the nonbinding of doubly negative ions to finitely many inequalities that we verify in a computer-assisted proof.

papers.title: Smale's sixth problem for six bodies in the plane: finiteness of central configurations for generic masses, with a proof formalized in Lean
papers.abstract: Smale's sixth problem asks whether, for every choice of positive masses, the number of central configurations up to similarity is finite. We prove that it is finite for six bodies in the plane and all positive masses outside a proper algebraic subset of the mass space. This subset, which we describe only in part, contains every mass vector with three equal masses or with one mass equal to the sum of two others. Finiteness for all positive masses remains open. Infinitely many central configurations would give a curve of complex solutions; following Albouy and Kaloshin, we exclude such a curve using the valuations of the mutual distances at its points at infinity. The proof is computer-assisted and uses linear programs, Gröbner bases and interval arithmetic. The theorem is proved in the Lean proof assistant, whose kernel checks the computations as well.

papers.title: Some positivity properties of Riemann $\Xi$ under smoothing
papers.abstract: We show that smoothing the zeros of the Riemann $\Xi$-function makes it easy to establish positivity properties that are otherwise hard (as they are equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis). Specifically, we smooth each zero with a small density centered at it, and then test the impact of this smoothing on complete monotonicity (CM) of the heat sum $H(t)=\sum_\rho e^{-tz_\rho^2}$ over the zeros $\tfrac12+iz_\rho$. A sufficiently wide density quickly implies CM of the smoothed heat sum. We bound the width (i.e., half-variance) the density needs using increasingly precise facts about the zeros. If we only use that they lie in the critical strip, half-variance $1/8$ suffices; the primes lower this width to $\pi^2/288$; and zeros verified through height $T$ further lower it to $\pi^2/(8\log^2T)$ asymptotically. Ultimately, however, smoothing seems to be of limited utility: despite the CM result, the smoothed reciprocal laws of $\Xi$ are not even log-concave, unlike the unsmoothed ones.

papers.title: Sorting networks on 13 inputs need at least 44 comparators
papers.abstract: Let $S(N)$ be the least number of comparators in a sorting network on $N$ inputs. We prove $S(13)\ge44$, one more than the previously best proved lower bound. We also prove $P(2,N)=\lceil \log_2 F(N)\rceil$ for $3\le N\le32$, where $P(2,N)$ is the least worst-case number of comparators met by the two largest inputs in a network that delivers them to fixed outputs and $F$ is an explicit function of Van Voorhis; the lower bound comes from a finite search based on the structure of the paths of these two values. Starting from Harder's $S(11)=35$ and $S(12)=39$, these values of $P(2,N)$, the two-value bound $S(N)\ge S(N-2)+P(2,N)$ and the one-value bound $S(N)\ge S(N-1)+\lceil \log_2 N\rceil$ give the twenty lower bounds on $S(N)$ for $13\le N\le32$ in Dobbelaere's table; these bounds rested on Van Voorhis's inequality $P(2,N)\ge\lceil \log_2 F(N)\rceil$, whose published proof is invalid. The bound $S(13)\ge44$ is also proved in Lean 4, with every step checked by Lean's kernel.

papers.title: Stability conditions on twisted derived categories I: Existence and full numerical support
papers.abstract: We prove that for every nonempty smooth projective variety $X$ over an arbitrary field and every Brauer class $\alpha$, the twisted derived category $\mathrm{D}^b(X,\alpha)$ admits a Bridgeland stability condition with full numerical support. Based on Chunyi Li's construction and its extension to arbitrary fields, we establish uniform phase control under tensoring by an Azumaya algebra and calibrate the resulting slicing to the induced central charge. We further show that the constructed stability condition is geometric and satisfies a mass-Hom bound, which persists throughout its connected component.

papers.title: Subplanes of order 3 and maximal arcs in projective planes of order 12
papers.abstract: Whether a projective plane of order 12 exists is open. A subplane of order 3 of such a plane is a case of equality in Bruck's bound $n\ge m^2+m$; the 27 points on no line of the subplane then form a maximal arc of degree 3, and together with the subplane a maximal arc $K$ of degree 4.
