We show that every line of a subplane of order 3 contained in $K$ lies in at most two such subplanes, whereas in $\mathrm{PG}(3,3)$, which like $K$ has 40 points, a line lies in four planes; the proof uses Egan and Wanless's classification of triples of mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order 9. We also show that $\mathrm{AG}(3,3)$ is not the design of any maximal arc of degree 3 in a plane of order 12, and that a permutation of the points that maps a subplane of order 3 onto itself and each line meeting it onto a line cannot have prime order other than 3. The proofs are computer-assisted, and their SAT refutations are certified.

papers.title: Supersymmetric Analysis of a Random Band Matrix at Criticality, Volume I
papers.abstract: We study the $N \times N$ complex Hermitian Gaussian band matrix whose variance profile is the inverse of $I - W^2 \Delta$, where $\Delta$ is the Neumann Laplacian on $\{1, \dots, N\}$, in the critical regime $W^2 \asymp N$. We prove that, for energies $E$ in a neighborhood of zero, the unfolded eigenvalue process converges to a stationary point process, whose law depends only on the limit $X$ of $N/((4 - E^2) W^2)$ and is given by the partition functions of a supersymmetric sigma model on an interval. We also determine the macroscopic law of the mass of an eigenvector selected near a given energy. Its density is the normalized exponential of a Brownian motion with drift, under the law tilted by its total mass; the same law describes the eigenvectors of the critical one-dimensional random Schrödinger operator. Further, we compute the limits of the two-energy correlations of the local densities of states at all pairs of interior sites, of the mean eigenvector profile at the scale of single sites, and of $N$ times the mean inverse participation ratio, which is $2 + 2X/3$. As $X \to 0$ and $X \to \infty$, we recover the pair statistics of the GUE and of a Poisson process, and in the localized limit we obtain an explicit random shape for the eigenvectors. The number variance in a window of length $L$ grows like $\sqrt{XL}$ as $L \to \infty$ at every fixed $X$, and we describe the crossover to Poisson statistics in windows of length of order $X$. Several of these results confirm predictions that physicists obtained from the sigma model. The proof starts from the supersymmetric representation of averages of ratios of characteristic polynomials, which for this profile is a transfer operator on a one-dimensional chain. We show that the transfer chain converges to the heat semigroup of the sigma model, whose noncompact direction produces the Brownian motion in the eigenvector law.

papers.title: The 24-cell conjecture in the all-contact case and near D4
papers.abstract: The 24-cell conjecture states that every Voronoi cell of a packing of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has volume at least $8$, the volume of the regular 24-cell. It implies that no packing of equal balls in $\mathbb{R}^4$ is denser than the lattice packing $D_4$. We prove the conjecture for two classes of cells; in each class, equality holds only for the $D_4$ root configuration. The first consists of the cells whose ball touches every ball centred at distance less than $2\sqrt2$ from its centre, and its proof uses a certificate at the second level of the Lasserre hierarchy. The second consists of the cells whose $24$ nearest centres lie in an explicit neighbourhood of the $D_4$ configuration, whatever the other centres are. For them the volume is at least $8$ plus a fixed multiple of the total outward displacement of the $24$ centres, which we prove by a quantitative rigidity estimate and a second-order expansion of the volume about $D_4$. Our proofs for both classes are computer-assisted and partly formalised in Lean.

papers.title: The automorphism group of an extremal [72,36,16] code is trivial
papers.abstract: Whether a binary doubly-even self-dual $[72,36,16]$ code exists is a question raised by Sloane in 1973. A series of papers, surveyed by Borello, shows that the automorphism group of such a code is trivial or isomorphic to $C_2$, $C_3$, $C_2\times C_2$ or $C_5$. We prove that such a code has no automorphism of order $2$, $3$ or $5$, and hence no nontrivial automorphism. Each such automorphism reduces the problem to a finite computer search. For order $2$ the search runs over symmetric bilinear forms on the $41$ self-dual $[36,18,8]$ codes. An automorphism of order $3$ leads to a search over labellings of the Hermitian self-dual $[24,12,8]$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_4$ by the extended Golay code. Order $5$ reduces to $7\times7$ unitary matrices over $\mathbb{F}_{16}$. Along the way we classify the Hermitian self-dual $[24,12,8]$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_4$: there are $26\,924\,931$ of them up to monomial equivalence.

papers.title: The classic enumeration of genera of even definite lattices
papers.abstract: We revisit the enumeration of a genus of even positive definite lattices by Kneser neighbours, certified by the mass. We work at primes dividing the determinant, where the projective spaces are smallest, schedule the exploration of the neighbour graph by a random walk and by orders based on a Hecke bookkeeping, and compute canonical forms through the Weyl chamber of the root system. Genera of rank up to 19 with up to 40,617 classes are enumerated in minutes.

papers.title: The Cranston–Li–Su–Wang–Xu (2026) conjecture is true
papers.abstract: Let A be a finite abelian group. A nowhere-zero A-flow of a graph can be changed along a cycle: going around the cycle, add a fixed non-zero element of A to the value of every edge that points forward and subtract it from the value of every edge that points backward. The Cranston–Li–Su–Wang–Xu (2026) conjecture on the reconfiguration of nowhere-zero flows states that if A has at least four elements, then in every graph in which all degrees are even, any two nowhere-zero A-flows are joined by a chain of such changes through nowhere-zero A-flows. It also states that, for every integer k ≥ 4, the same holds for integer flows whose values are between 1 and k − 1 in absolute value, where each change adds a non-zero integer. We prove this conjecture. The proof is by induction on the number of edges. If a flow enters a vertex along one edge and leaves it along another edge with the same value, the two edges can be replaced by a single edge; this gives a smaller graph. The main step is to change every flow into a flow with such a pair of edges. For A-flows we do this when all degrees are at most 4; repeatedly replacing a vertex of degree at least 6 by a triangle, following Cranston et al., reduces the general case to this one. For integer flows, we show that, in a graph in which all degrees are even, any two nowhere-zero flows with values in the cyclic group Z_k, k ≥ 4, are joined by changes that add only 1, −1, 2 or −2, and that such changes lift to integer flows. All theorems of this paper are also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

papers.title: The exact diameter of the symmetric group 𝑆𝑛 with LRX generators
papers.abstract: We consider the undirected Cayley graph of the symmetric group 𝑆𝑛 with respect to the cyclic shift 𝐿, its inverse 𝑅, and the transposition 𝑋 of the first two positions. We prove that its diameter is given by 𝑛(𝑛 − 1)/2 for every 𝑛 ≥ 4, thus settling a conjecture open since at least 2011. This is done by separately establishing sharp upper and lower bounds, invoking a variety of combinatorial and group-theoretic arguments which leave a finite set of special cases that are verified in the accompanying C++ code. We also provide a Lean formalization of the results.

papers.title: The Humphreys support conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Humphreys support conjecture for connected reductive groups over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>h$.

papers.title: The independence number of the generalized Johnson graph $J(13,5,3)$
papers.abstract: Let $J(13,5,3)$ be the graph on the 5-element subsets of a 13-element set, two subsets being adjacent when they share exactly 3 elements. We prove that $\alpha(J(13,5,3)) = 33$. The graph is an explicit unit-distance graph in $\mathbb{R}^{12}$, so $\chi(\mathbb{R}^{12}) \ge \lceil 1287/33 \rceil = 39$; earlier bounds from explicit finite graphs give at most 38. A recent preprint of Davies gives much larger bounds, none from an explicit finite graph. An explicit independent set gives $\alpha \ge 33$. For the upper bound, a symmetry reduction splits the problem into 200 clique subproblems, and a certifying solver refutes each one with a proof log that the checker VeriPB accepts. An uncertified computation reproduces the value $\alpha(J(13,6,4)) = 46$ reported by Exoo and Ismailescu, which gives $\chi(\mathbb{R}^{12}) \ge 38$.

papers.title: The kissing numbers in dimensions five and seven are at most 43 and 132
papers.abstract: The kissing number $\tau_n$ is the largest number of non-overlapping unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^n$ that can touch a common unit ball. The best bounds so far were $40\le\tau_5\le44$ and $126\le\tau_7\le134$; both upper bounds come from high-precision floating-point computations of the three-point bound by Mittelmann and Vallentin. We prove $\tau_5\le 43$ and $\tau_7\le132$. Each proof is an exact rational solution of the second level of the Lasserre hierarchy for spherical codes at degrees $(d_1,d_2,\delta)=(14,20,20)$. We use the formulation of de Laat, Leijenhorst and de Muinck Keizer and check the solutions with their verification program. Each certificate is obtained by rounding a convex combination of two dual iterates of the interior-point method, one on each side of the target value. Exact certificates for the same hierarchy also give $A(4,\arccos\frac13)\le14$, $A(5,\arccos\frac13)\le22$ and $A(6,\arccos\frac13)\le34$ for spherical codes, improving the previous bounds $15$, $23$ and $35$; with a known code, $A(4,\arccos\frac13)=14$. The largest number of points at angle $\pi/3$ from a point of a kissing configuration in $\mathbb{R}^n$ equals $A(n-1,\arccos\frac13)$, so in $\mathbb{R}^5$ this number is $14$. We also prove the five bounds in the Lean proof assistant, assuming only the positivity of the zonal kernels given by the zonal polynomial files: once by checking the exact certificates with compiled code, and once, with every computation done by Lean's kernel, from the certificates rounded to $30$ decimal places.

papers.title: The L¹ Poincaré constant of the Hamming cube
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be the smallest constant such that $\mathbb{E}|f-\mathbb{E} f|\le C\,\mathbb{E}|\nabla f|$ for every real-valued function $f$ on every Hamming cube $\{-1,1\}^n$, where $|\nabla f|$ is the Euclidean length of $(D_1f,\dots,D_nf)$ and $D_jf(x)=(f(x)-f(x^{(j)}))/2$. Ben Efraim and Lust-Piquard proved $C\le\pi/2$, the Gaussian case gives $C\ge\sqrt{\pi/2}$, and Ivanisvili, Li, van Handel and Volberg asked whether $C=\sqrt{\pi/2}$. We prove that it is, with an explicit constant $c_n<\sqrt{\pi/2}$ in dimension $n$. The proof turns on an integral of first absolute moments of sums of independent biased random signs: we compute it exactly when the coefficients are nonnegative, and show, with a sampled Fejér kernel, that it can only grow when the coefficients are replaced by their absolute values. The equality $C=\sqrt{\pi/2}$ is also proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: The Marcus-Minc Transform Inequality
papers.abstract: We prove the Marcus-Minc conjecture: let n be any integer at least 2, and let A be a nonnegative n by n matrix whose row and column sums are all one. Form a new matrix by subtracting A from the n by n matrix of ones and dividing by n minus one. Then the permanent of A is at least the permanent of the new matrix. We also determine all equality cases.

papers.title: The Maximum of $\operatorname{per}(I-A)$ in Odd Order
papers.abstract: Let $Ω_n$ denote the set of $n\times n$ doubly stochastic matrices. Kim and Roush conjectured in 1981 that, for $n=2k+1>1$, $ \max_{A\inΩ_{2k+1}}\operatorname{per}(I-A)=3\cdot 2^{k-2}$. They proposed the block construction $A_\star=\frac12(J_3-I_3)\oplus P_2^{\oplus(k-1)}$, where $P_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Here $J_3$ is the $3\times3$ all-ones matrix. They did not claim uniqueness. We fully prove their conjecture and classify equality: the maximizers are exactly the simultaneous-permutation conjugates of $A_\star$.

papers.title: The Maximum Permanent of a Stochastic Matrix of Bounded Rank
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a stochastic $n\times n$ matrix with $\operatorname{rank}A\leq k$, where $1\leq k\leq n$. Write $n=qk+s$, where $0\leq s<k$. The author conjectured in 2018 that $\operatorname{per}A\leq (q!/q^q)^{k-s}((q+1)!/(q+1)^{q+1})^s$, with equality if and only if $A=P(J_q^{\oplus(k-s)}\oplus J_{q+1}^{\oplus s})Q$, where $P,Q$ are permutation matrices and $J_t$ is the $t\times t$ matrix with every entry $1/t$. We prove this conjecture in full.

papers.title: The number of planar central configurations of four bodies
papers.abstract: For four positive masses in the plane we determine the number $N$ of central configurations, counted up to rotation, translation and scaling, in terms of one fold surface, whose certified enclosures decide $N$ for all masses outside a closed null set. Of these configurations, $12$ are collinear, by Moulton's theorem, and $6$ are convex, by the existence theorem of MacMillan and Bartky and the uniqueness proved in the author's preprint arXiv:2609.35632. Through Dziobek's relations, the concave configurations with inner body $i$ form the fibre of a proper mass map of degree $2$. Their number $c_i$, counted up to reflection, is $1$, $2$, $3$ or $4$, and we read it off from the position of the mass ratios relative to this surface. Altogether $N=18+2(c_1+c_2+c_3+c_4)$, an even number with $32\le N\le50$. Moreover $N=32$ exactly at Palmore's masses, and every even value in this range occurs. For four equal masses we recover Albouy's count $N=50$. The proof shows with interval certificates that the mass map is injective where its Jacobian is not positive, obtains its degree from the restricted problem, and analyses its folds, cusps and Palmore's umbilic. A formalization in Lean also proves these results.

papers.title: The PPT² conjecture holds for spin-factor maps
papers.abstract: The PPT$^2$ conjecture asserts that the composition of two completely positive and completely copositive maps is entanglement breaking. A counterexample in dimension ten has recently been announced, and for maps on $\mathrm{M}_4$ the conjecture is open. Let $\mathcal{S}\subset\mathrm{M}_4$ be the real span of the identity $\gamma_0$ and five pairwise anticommuting Hermitian unitaries $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_5$. It is a spin factor whose positive cone is a Lorentz cone. We prove the conjecture for all compositions $\Psi\circ\Phi$ of completely positive maps $\Phi\colon\mathrm{M}_4\to\mathrm{M}_k$ and $\Psi\colon\mathrm{M}_k\to\mathrm{M}_4$, with $k$ arbitrary, such that the ranges of $\Psi$ and of the adjoint $\Phi^{*}$ lie in invertible congruences of the complex span of $\mathcal{S}$. Such maps are automatically completely copositive, and the class contains maps whose Choi matrices are entangled. A theorem of Hildebrand on separability for pairs of Lorentz cones reduces the claim to one trace inequality between the coefficient matrices of the two Choi matrices. We derive this inequality from the operator inequality $\sum_{j=1}^{5}F_jF_0^{-1}F_j\preceq F_0$, valid whenever $\sum_{\mu=0}^{5}F_\mu\otimes\gamma_\mu\succeq 0$ and $F_0\succ 0$, which in turn follows from the Kadison–Schwarz inequality. As a corollary, $\Psi\circ\Phi$ is entanglement breaking whenever $\Psi$ is such a map and $\Phi$ is a completely positive map with Kraus operators of rank at most two.

papers.title: The Quantum Kazhdan–Lusztig Conjecture for Quantum Loop Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the quantum Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture for finite-dimensional type 1 representations of untwisted quantum loop algebras at every non-root-of-unity complex parameter.

papers.title: The rank of 4×4 matrix multiplication over F2 is at least 35
papers.abstract: We prove that the rank of the $4\times4$ matrix multiplication tensor over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is at least $35$; the previous lower bound was $34$. The bound follows by substitution from $\mathrm{R}_{\mathbb{F}_2}(\langle 3,3,4\rangle)\ge27$, which also gives $\mathrm{R}_{\mathbb{F}_2}(\langle 3,4,4\rangle)\ge31$. Each of the three bounds is one more than what follows from $\mathrm{R}_{\mathbb{F}_2}(\langle 3,3,3\rangle)=23$. A flattening argument reduces the bound for $\langle 3,3,4\rangle$ to lower bounds for two quotients of the tensor, by the span of a matrix of rank two and by the span of a matrix of rank three. These come from exhaustive searches over the possible patterns of a short decomposition, pruned by lower bounds for quotients by larger subspaces. The whole argument, including every step of the searches, is checked in the proof assistant Lean 4, with one compiled evaluation of a verified certificate checker.

papers.title: The Steiner ratio is at least 0.8564
papers.abstract: The Steiner ratio is the infimum, over finite sets of points in the Euclidean plane, of the length of a Steiner minimal tree divided by the length of a minimum spanning tree. Gilbert and Pollak conjectured in 1968 that it equals $\sqrt3/2\approx0.8660$, and the conjecture is open. We prove that it is at least $2141/2500=0.8564$, improving the bound $0.8559$ of Ke, Huang, Shu, He, Gai and Wang. Their method reduces the induction step of Du and Hwang's 1983 proof of the bound $0.8$ to finitely many inequalities on boxes in a space of local configurations of a Steiner minimal tree, which are checked by computer. These inequalities use estimates for the positions of terminals outside the local configuration. We prove all the geometric lemmas that our certificate uses, filling gaps in two proofs of Ke et al., and we add two such estimates that hold for more parameter values than the published ones. Within this method some new estimate is necessary: with the published estimates, no certificate of this kind reaches $0.856$, whatever the boxes. The computer-assisted part is also verified in Lean 4, by a proof whose checks all run in Lean's kernel; the rest of the argument enters the formal proof as hypotheses.

papers.title: The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem
papers.abstract: This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for It\^o diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem. More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehat\mu_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i\delta_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehat\mu_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$. In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehat\mu_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2\lambda_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2\lambda_d}$, where $\lambda_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.

papers.title: Unitary character moments and a zero-free half-plane for unitary Weil L-functions
papers.abstract: We extend Liu's moment estimate for ordinary ideal-character sums to two independent fixed unitary twists, preserving the full length range of the finite-order theorem. The proof keeps the two character coefficients separate through the Gauss transformations and controls exceptional terms by the poles of their Mellin transforms. The case of two equal twists strengthens the fourth moment used in zero detection. Using the analytic results of Hu and Liu specified in the paper, we obtain the zero-free half-plane $\operatorname{Re}s>(777-\sqrt{1081})/852=0.8733819666\ldots$ for every unitary Hecke $L$-function over every number field, including characters of infinite order. This extends the known finite-order bound to the full unitary family. Unitary induction gives the same half-plane for finite-dimensional continuous unitary Weil representations, with the norm-character poles counted exactly.

papers.title: Which Fine-Grained Lower Bounds Survive the Refutation of 3SUM and APSP?
papers.abstract: Alman and Vassilevska Williams have refuted the 3SUM and APSP hypotheses. Their algorithms rest on counting the triangles through prescribed edges of lopsided tripartite graphs, whose middle part has $n^{\varepsilon}$ vertices for a small $\varepsilon$. Majdoddin extended the method to every $\varepsilon<\ln4/(5\ln5)\approx0.172$. We determine which of the main conditional lower bounds derived from the refuted hypotheses survive. We also prove that the method extends to every $\varepsilon<0.17843$ when the prescribed edges are known in advance and there are at most $n^{2-\varepsilon/2}$ of them, which confirms Majdoddin's numerical estimate. Whether a bound survives depends mostly on the instances that its reduction produces. The reductions behind most bounds produce instances outside the range of the new algorithms: balanced graphs, or lopsided graphs with a larger middle part. Most of the set-disjointness, dynamic-graph and triangle bounds therefore follow from hypotheses that no known algorithm contradicts. These hypotheses, however, concern mainly such instances, and for several bounds the hypothesis is the bound itself, stated for these instances. Their evidence came largely from the refuted hypotheses. A few bounds are false, among them a lower bound of Goldstein, Lewenstein and Porat for Set Disjointness over small universes; the Strong SetDisjointness Conjecture also fails at small polynomial query times. Other bounds have lost their support, such as the Set Disjointness trade-offs of Kopelowitz, Pettie and Porat over small universes apart from constant query time. Finally, we collect the known obstacles to a larger closed-form range with a different base identity and use border-rank lower bounds to exclude several natural candidates.
